notes: This resource is the Google Benchmark C++ microbenchmark library. Its package smoke timings are not an official compiler Benchmark score and are not evidence of performance improvement.
The distribution profile uses static libraries, C++17, x86-64 baseline code, exceptions enabled and LTO disabled. It preserves the full upstream source and original selector recipe.

GoogleTest-based unit tests, LLVM assembly verification, Rust bindings and libpfm/physical performance counters are not enabled in this profile. Their sources and upstream build options remain available; their qualification is not claimed.
CMake/Ninja are build-only. Matching pinned system tools use the normal path; the maintainer replay can use exact locked private Debian packages as explicit build bindings without an APT transaction.

The installed pkg-config prefix is changed to ${pcfiledir}/../..; upstream library/test source files remain unmodified. CMake imports and prebuilt tests are checked at independent installation prefixes.
The Python comparison scripts are retained as upstream materials. They require the Python dependencies listed in tools/requirements.txt and are not claimed as a ready Python distribution.
For the locked source archive, Git-based version discovery is disabled so an enclosing framework checkout cannot replace the upstream CMake project version.
usage.summary: Native microbenchmark fixtures with anti-elimination helpers, repetitions and structured result output.

notes: This exact resource requires the existing py.psutil resource in the same selected Python environment. Use the environment interpreter; no shell activation is needed.
The functional check uses the official Runner for two workers with three measured values each, validates raw samples and public statistics, round-trips JSON, and rejects a failing external command.

The small qualification workload checks the tool protocol; it does not establish statistically stable performance. Keep Runner defaults or explicitly choose an experimental sampling policy for research.
CPU affinity, isolation and optional system tuning are researcher decisions. No tuning or system-wide configuration change is needed for these examples or the functional check.
pyperf is a measurement helper. It does not replace an independent Benchmark adapter's official timer, correctness checks, inputs or aggregation.
A payload-free wrapper forwards installation/removal to pip. Wheel bytes and wrapper bytes have separate exact identities; removing the distribution preserves its Python environment.
usage.summary: Run Python functions or external commands with the official pyperf worker/calibration protocol, retain raw JSON, inspect metadata and compare distributions.
